snippet.title: Which brands get AI localization right? Autos and streamers, explained
snippet.description:
From 'AI in action: Building smarter, scalable workflows', Canva's webinar with NBCUniversal, RWS and SoDA. How do top brands localize marketing across global markets? Michael Dobell, Vice Chair of SoDA Digital Society, tells Canva's Meghan Gendelman why autos and streamers set the bar. Streaming platforms test hundreds of creative variants per title. Automakers apply the same data-driven personalization across every touchpoint, from in-car marketing to CRM. Both build a customer taxonomy, a database of how customers live, work, and play, gathered like a retail team on the floor, then use it to guide pluggable production pipelines, so teams can swap in a translation, cultural-nuance, or image tool at low cost, with governance stepping in at scale and ways of working documented in code, not left in people's heads. From Canva's webinar, AI in Action: Building Smarter, Scalable Workflows. 

Two specifics worth surfacing: the taxonomy method mirrors retail, listening to what customers say on the floor, then systemizing and distributing that understanding globally. And the pluggable pipeline names three specific levers, translation, cultural nuance, and image generation, each swappable without rebuilding the whole system.

Key quotes
0:00 The question: what does market-ready localization look like in practice
0:23 Answer: autos and streamers set the bar
0:41 Streaming proof: one poster is actually one of hundreds of variants
1:08 The method: build a customer taxonomy, then let it guide the pipeline
1:41 Why pipelines stay pluggable, and where governance fits

snippet.title: How do global brands localize AI content without losing trust? NBCUniversal, RWS and SoDA
snippet.description:
Panel chat from 'AI in action: Building smarter, scalable workflows', Canva's webinar with NBCUniversal, RWS and SoDA. How do global brands localize AI content without losing trust? The panel's answer: translation is mostly solved, culture is not. Content breaks when brand voice, idioms, calls to action and compliance cross markets unchecked, which is why 86% of teams say AI accelerated creation while 65% say localization slowed, with about 20% of effort spent on corrections. NBCUniversal's Catie Liken, RWS's Matt Hardy and SoDA vice chair Michael Dobell share what works: customer taxonomies driving pluggable creative pipelines, creative variation matched to context, and AI treated as infrastructure so creatives spend time on strategy and taste instead of resizing.

Speakers: Meghan Gendelman (CMO B2B, Canva), Catie Liken (VP Creative Technology, NBCUniversal), Matt Hardy (SVP, RWS Group), Michael Dobell (Vice Chair, SoDA - till May 2026).

Covered: localization, cultural intelligence, customer taxonomy, creative variation, AI infrastructure, connected TV templates.

snippet.title: Why does AI content feel generic? NBCUniversal, RWS and SoDA on what top brands do differently
snippet.description:
Full panel topics from 'AI in action: Building smarter, scalable workflows', Canva's webinar with NBCUniversal, RWS and SoDA. Why does AI content feel generic, and what do top brands do differently? The panel's answer: AI raised the execution baseline, so differentiation now comes from strategy, taste and cultural intelligence, the parts teams skip when chasing volume. NBCUniversal's Catie Liken, RWS's Matt Hardy and SoDA vice chair Michael Dobell join Canva B2B CMO Meghan Gendelman to unpack AI slop, why 70% of consumers say they can tell when content is AI generated, and how leading teams move from AI as a tool to governed creative pipelines. 97% of marketing leaders already use AI daily and 41% call AI slop a considerable challenge. The gap is not adoption, it is what you do with the time AI saves.

Speakers: Meghan Gendelman (CMO B2B, Canva), Catie Liken (VP Creative Technology, NBCUniversal), Matt Hardy (SVP, RWS Group), Michael Dobell (Vice Chair, SoDA - till May 2026).

Covered: AI slop, differentiation, taste, localization, cultural intelligence, creative pipelines, governance.

snippet.title: How do you turn AI adoption into real impact? AI in action: Building smarter, scalable workflows
snippet.description:
How do you scale AI powered content globally without losing your brand? This full webinar answers in two parts: a panel on why AI accelerated content often fails to land, and a live Canva demo going from campaign idea to marketing brief to roughly 50 localized assets. The panel's short answer: keep strategy and taste human, treat localization as cultural intelligence rather than translation, and move AI from a point tool to governed marketing infrastructure. Canva research shows 97% of marketing leaders already use AI daily and 89% save at least four hours a week, yet 65% say localization has slowed and about 20% of effort goes to fixing weak translations. The differentiator is no longer speed, it is judgment.

Speakers: Meghan Gendelman (CMO B2B, Canva), Catie Liken (VP Creative Technology, NBCUniversal), Matt Hardy (SVP, RWS Group), Michael Dobell (Vice Chair, SoDA - till May 2026), Kevin Mengual (Canva EMEA).

Topics covered: AI slop, cultural intelligence, localization, creative pipelines, brand governance, content factory, bulk creation.

snippet.title: How do you go from campaign idea to marketing brief to 50 localized assets in Canva?
snippet.description:
Demo clips from 'AI in action: Building smarter, scalable workflows', Canva's webinar with NBCUniversal, RWS and SoDA. How do you go from a campaign idea to a marketing brief to roughly 50 localized assets without leaving Canva? Kevin Mengual from Canva EMEA shows the full workflow: Canva AI drafts the brief by pulling context from Slack, a campaign workspace holds the brief, templates and a content factory spreadsheet, Bulk Create turns 16 spreadsheet rows into about 50 on brand assets across markets and formats, components push a design fix to every asset at once, and Canva builds a results presentation straight from a CSV. This is what AI as marketing infrastructure looks like in day to day work: the marketer stays on strategy while production runs at scale.

Speaker: Kevin Mengual (Canva EMEA), from Canva's AI in Action webinar hosted by Meghan Gendelman (CMO B2B, Canva).

Covered: campaign brief, Canva AI, Slack integration in Canva, campaign workspace, content factory, Bulk Create, components, brand templates, presentations from data.

snippet.title: Courage Beats Fear of New Tools
snippet.description:
What if the same fears people had about writing, the printing press, and the telephone are the exact fears we have about AI today?

Debbie Millman, designer, author, educator, and host of the pioneering podcast Design Matters, joins Cameron Adams to talk about creativity, technology, and why humans have always been afraid of the next big tool. From branding icons like Burger King and Tropicana to interviewing over 700 of the world's most creative minds, Debbie brings decades of perspective to the question everyone in design is asking right now.

In this episode, they explore why AI panic follows the same pattern as every past technological shift, how design students are using AI to reimagine legacy brands like Archie Comics, why Debbie is more worried about young people's brains than about job loss, and why original thought will always be the one thing AI can't generate.

snippet.title: The Natural Progression of AI in Design: Insights from Debbie Millman
snippet.description:
What if the same fears people had about writing, the printing press, and the telephone are the exact fears we have about AI today?

Debbie Millman, designer, author, educator, and host of the pioneering podcast Design Matters, joins Cameron Adams to talk about creativity, technology, and why humans have always been afraid of the next big tool. From branding icons like Burger King and Tropicana to interviewing over 700 of the world's most creative minds, Debbie brings decades of perspective to the question everyone in design is asking right now.

In this episode, they explore why AI panic follows the same pattern as every past technological shift, how design students are using AI to reimagine legacy brands like Archie Comics, why Debbie is more worried about young people's brains than about job loss, and why original thought will always be the one thing AI can't generate. Plus: a childhood doodle rooted in Debbie's inability to draw the letter H gets transformed live by AI and Canva's design team into a piece that reveals the origin of her nickname.

Key Quotes
“We can't even pinpoint the origins of our own consciousness. I am not worried at all about computers becoming sentient in the next century.”
“I'm more worried about students' brains not being able to craft certain things on their own before going to AI.”
“The tenets of branding for potato chips and fast food are the same tenets [of] MeToo, Black Lives Matter, Time's Up. People are using those tenets to change behavior, which I don't think AI can do yet.”
“There's no technology  where there wasn't some backlash. If we look at that pattern, it could make us less afraid of this tool and more empowered to leverage it for our creativity.”

Timestamps
00:00 Introduction
02:08 The Prompt
06:04 Creative All Hands
07:22 Even Socrates and Plato feared writing itself, worried it would destroy human memory.
10:23 “Computers are to design as microwaves are to cooking.” - Milton Glaser
12:32 Every wave of design panic predicted doom for the craft. The opposite kept happening.
15:50 AI can sharpen research, but it can't write questions with soul.
18:11 Working on a draft table before the computer age gave Debbie a lifelong advantage: craft.
22:43 AI-assisted writing can be phenomenal, as long as it’s a start, not a substitute for original thought.
31:28 Canva’s philosophy: amplify human creativity – but amplifying requires an original starting point that’s inherently human.

snippet.title: Introducing the Canva Goals Platform, to find out where our hopes overlap
snippet.description:

👉 Read more: https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/global-goals/

USA Goals, in partnership with the Ad Council, pairs open public participation with nationally representative research to build a true picture of American ambition – across communities, geographies, and backgrounds that don't always get to sit at the same table. Americans can submit their goal at usagoals.org.

Wollongong Goals, in partnership with Wollongong City Council, will invite the 220,000 residents of the city to share what they want to see for their community. Wollongong residents can submit their goals at wollongonggoals.org

snippet.title: Michele Catasta on Vibe Coding, Replit Agent, and the Future of Software Development
snippet.description:
What if the tools to build the next billion-dollar company are already in your hands and you don't need to write a single line of code?
Michele Catasta, President and Head of AI at Replit, joins Cameron Adams to talk about the vibe coding revolution, what it means to build software in the age of AI agents, and why the future belongs to people with great taste, not just great technical skills. From applying transformers to source code before anyone knew what to do with them, to architecting Replit Agent and helping drive 100x revenue growth, Michele has spent his career at Stanford, Google X, and now Replit at the intersection of deep research and real-world building.
In this episode, they explore why vibe coding is too small a term for what's really happening, what makes the one-person unicorn possible, why taste and agency are the defining skills of the AI era, and what an "AI chief of staff" actually does. Plus: a childhood sketch of aviator glasses gets transformed into something far more cinematic by Canva's designer in residence.

Key Quotes
“The human taste, the understanding of what to build, how to build it, at which time it should be done, that should still come from the person who's running the process.”
“ There is one very important trait that determines everyone's career, which is openness to receive feedback, know how to internalize it, and not to take it in a defensive way, but rather as a way to grow yourself.”
“We all took inspiration from what has been done in the past. You inspire yourself, you remix it, and then you create a new artistic language. The same is happening with AI.”
“You can think of agents in the future allowing you to figure out your legal concerns, creating your entity, contacting investors, and doing everything that you need in order to run a company correctly.”

01:46 The Prompt
03:53 Creative All Hands

19:04 AI has become a true sidekick – always there, across every part of your role, not just the technical ones.
22:31 The best way to measure how fast AI is improving: notice how much more you rely on it month over month.
29:36 The new AI chief of staff: someone who can mingle with every team AND build.
34:04 Taste grows through feedback cycles. Now those cycles are weekly instead of quarterly.

snippet.title: Ideas Are the Currency of Today
snippet.description:
What if the journalist asking the hardest questions about AI has to face them himself?

Alex Kantrowitz, founder of Big Technology and one of tech's most trusted voices, joins Cameron Adams for a candid conversation about what it really looks like to cover, use, and build inside the AI revolution.

From cold-emailing his way into BuzzFeed to breaking the story that foreshadowed ChatGPT, Alex brings the same sharp, ground-level insight to this conversation that's made him a must-read for 150,000+ newsletter subscribers and millions of podcast listeners worldwide.

This conversation goes deep on what AI adoption actually looks like inside companies, inside media, and inside the tools we use every day.

snippet.title: Big Technology’s Alex Kantrowitz on Media in the AI Era, and Asking AI Leaders the Hard Questions
snippet.description:
What if the journalist asking the hardest questions about AI has to face them himself?
Alex Kantrowitz, founder of Big Technology and one of tech's most trusted voices, joins Cameron Adams for a candid conversation about what it really looks like to cover, use, and build inside the AI revolution.
From cold-emailing his way into BuzzFeed to breaking the story that foreshadowed ChatGPT, Alex brings the same sharp, ground-level insight to this conversation that's made him a must-read for 150,000+ newsletter subscribers and millions of podcast listeners worldwide.
This conversation goes deep on what AI adoption actually looks like inside companies, inside media, and inside the tools we use every day.
In this episode, they explore why fear remains the biggest obstacle to AI adoption and what separates companies that win from those that don't. They examine why generative AI produces the "average of averages" and how to inject a unique human seed to stand out. The conversation also covers why mandating AI usage percentages is a failure mode, and despite everything, why the future of media still belongs to humans.

Key Quotes
“If you say, this is a new technology, I don't understand it, I don't want to use it, I'm gonna stick to my processes, it can't help me — you're in trouble."
"There's something that you cannot replace with a machine, there's something human and connective about it. That will continue to be a very important medium no matter how much AI slop, or AI masterpieces, flood the system."
"The way these systems work is they take in content and try to predict the next word. That's all averages. When you prompt, you’re gonna get the average of all averages — which means it has a signature."
"Ideas are what matter. Execution is being automated, but ideas are what matter."

Timestamps
00:00 Introduction
02:00 The Prompt
06:41Creative All Hands
08:44 Cross-disciplinary experience makes you a sharper, more credible thinker.
14:37 Sometimes staying is riskier. A capped ceiling makes the “safe” path the dangerous one.
19:30 AI automates execution; ideas stay human. Invest in original thinking.
27:27 The only way to truly understand AI is to use it.  
32:52 Great interviews come from great reporting beforehand.
39:39 Don’t let fear of new technology paralyze you. Allow your team to adapt.
49:18 All Star Creative Team
51:23 Design Reveal
52:36 Rapid Fire

snippet.title: AI That Listens to Nature
snippet.description:
What if data isn't just information — but memory, pigment, and the raw material of a new art form?

Pioneering AI artist Refik Anadol joins Cameron to explore how machine intelligence, ethical data, and human creativity can come together to create experiences that move people — from record-breaking exhibitions at MoMA to Dataland, a living museum built from the ground up for the AI era.

This conversation goes deep on what it really means to collaborate with AI as a creative partner — and why the future of art isn't about replacement, but about finding what humans and machines can only do together.

snippet.title: What Happens When AI Learns from Nature
snippet.description:
What if data isn't just information — but memory, pigment, and the raw material of a new art form?

Pioneering AI artist Refik Anadol joins Cameron to explore how machine intelligence, ethical data, and human creativity can come together to create experiences that move people — from record-breaking exhibitions at MoMA to Dataland, a living museum built from the ground up for the AI era.

This conversation goes deep on what it really means to collaborate with AI as a creative partner — and why the future of art isn't about replacement, but about finding what humans and machines can only do together.

In this episode, they cover:
• Why data is memory and how Refik uses it as his creative pigment
• How training custom AI models on 500 million nature images unlocked a new art form
• How Dataland reimagines what a museum can be in the age of AI
• Why ethical and sustainable AI must be a creative practice
• What 50/50 human-machine collaboration actually looks like in the studio
• How Refik thinks about nature as the original living intelligence

Key Quotes
"To me, data is an invisible, poetic force or form of life in this new era of life."
“I see it as machine human collaboration — 50% machine, 50% human."
"I always see AI not as a replacement, but as a great friend that has a chance to help us. And I hope this doesn't change."
"If AI means anything and everything, it has to be for anyone and everyone."

Timestamps
00:26 Introduction
07:47 Ask unusual questions of your tools to discover entirely new creative territories.
15:44 Design technology so it disappears. The goal is to put humans at the center of the experience, not the hardware.
25:03 Use AI to unlock what human cognition cannot do alone, while keeping creative intent human-led.
30:44 Push into uncomfortable, unexplored territory — pioneering happens when you see beyond what any field thinks is possible.
35:48 If AI means anything and everything, make sure it's accessible to anyone and everyone.
37:18 All Star Creative Team
38:54 Rapid Fire

snippet.title: Turning AI Into Infrastructure with Atlassian’s Sherif Mansour
snippet.description:
Sherif Mansour has spent over 16 years at Atlassian helping shape products like Jira and Confluence. Now Head of AI at Atlassian, he’s focused on a bigger shift: how AI changes not just what we build, but how teams work together.

In this episode, Sherif and Cameron unpack why many organizations remain in “single-player mode” with AI, and why transformation happens when AI becomes part of collaborative workflows. Sherif shares how Atlassian deploys agents inside procurement, product, and customer feedback systems, why synchronized experimentation drives adoption, and why as AI accelerates output, strategy becomes more important, not less.

Key Quotes
“Don’t look for a killer AI use case. Look at what your team already does and make that better.”
“As AI speeds everything up, strategy matters more. You have to point the ship in the right direction.”

Timestamps
00:00 - Introduction
00:57 - The Prompt
02:51 - Creative All Hands
08:27 - Define "long term" in AI strategy as the next six months.
15:16 - Identify your stage in the AI maturity pyramid: answers, task execution, then virtual teammates.
20:59 - Map team workflows first, then insert AI agents at specific friction points.
24:00 - Celebrate failed experiments to encourage ambitious AI experimentation across teams.
30:50 - Expect humans to become the bottleneck as AI dramatically increases output.
34:30 - Give AI step-by-step instructions, not just the final task.
37:03 - All Star Creative Team
38:31 - Design Reveal

snippet.title: Why the Smartest Product Teams Are Letting Everyone Build
snippet.description:
AI is changing how products get built.

Superhuman CPO Noam Lovinsky joins Cameron Adams to discuss how AI is reshaping product development and why product teams are starting to look very different.

From Grammarly’s transformation into Superhuman to the changing role of product managers, Noam explains why the boundaries between design, engineering, and product are starting to blur.

In this episode they explore:

• Why chat may not be the ultimate interface for AI
• Why product managers may soon ship code themselves
• Why the hardest problem may no longer be building, but deciding what to build

Guest Quotes
“Very soon the expectation is that all PMs will be pushing code to production.”
“We had to disrupt ourselves and go after it — or pack our bags.”


Timestamps: 
00:00 Intro
01:30 The Prompt 
04:29 Creative All Hands 
09:56 Treat major AI shifts as a refounding moment for the company. 
12:46 "We had to basically disrupt ourselves and go after it, or pack our bags."
23:06 Chat is now a UX primitive, in the same way as a button or a dropdown is.
23:44 Create AI tools that work where people do: docs, code, designs 
24:23 Build AI canvases that actively write and create alongside the user.
29:37 Use AI to compress long meetings into clear summaries people can act on.
35:50 Create rituals like AI Fridays where teams share how they are using AI tools.
37:35 "Very soon the expectation is that all PMs will be pushing code to production."
37:52 “How can we make sure PMs can build an idea and get customer feedback within 24 hours?”
39:36 Smaller zero to one teams can succeed with AI tools. 
40:30 Start with the outcome you want when working with AI agents.
40:48 Create verification loops so AI systems can check their own work. 
43:22 Time saved with AI is a form of “life extension.” 
44:06 All-Star Creative Team 
46:00 Design Reveal 
47:23 Outro

Two designers. One wedding invitation brief. Completely different results.

In this episode of The Drawing Board, we sit two Canva designers down with the same wedding invitation copy - same names, same date, same venue, same details. The only thing that changes is the creative direction. One designs minimalist. One designs maximalist. They have 30 minutes, full access to Canva, and no idea what the other person is making.

Watch them work in real time. Hear how they think through every decision - color, typography, layout, imagery. Then we put both designs side by side and let the designers react to each other's work for the first time.

There's no winner. There's no "right" answer. Just a masterclass in how creative direction shapes everything.

snippet.title: This Changes How We Communicate at Work
snippet.description:
AI is transforming how we communicate and who gets to create.
HeyGen CTO Rong Yan joins Cameron to explore how AI avatars, video agents, and new creative tools are reshaping the future of work. From turning spreadsheets into videos in minutes to enabling anyone to create high-quality content, this conversation dives into a world where video becomes the default way we share ideas.
They also unpack a major mindset shift: why success in the AI era isn’t about accumulating knowledge, but adapting faster than ever before.

In this episode, they cover:
• Why “10x employees” are being redefined in the AI era
• How AI avatars are changing communication across teams
• Why video may replace text in the workplace
• The rise of AI companions and agent-powered workflows
• How to think about trust and authenticity in AI-generated content
• Why the real problem isn’t too much content but not enough good content

Guest Quotes
“I don’t believe in accumulation. What matters now is how fast you can learn and adapt.”
“A 10x person isn’t someone who knows more. It’s someone who can leverage tools better.”
“AI is not a replacement for humans. It’s a tool to improve the quality of humans.”
“It’s not about too much content. It’s about too little good content.”

This panel discusses the importance of data storytelling, emphasizing the need for clear presentation of evidence, highlighting uncertainties, and guiding insights. As AI manages production, the key human skills required are judgment, clarity, and aiding comprehension of the data's true message.

snippet.title: The MVB (Minimum Viable Brand) Framework
snippet.description: James Martin introduces his Most Viable Brand (MVB) framework, a straightforward way to build brands that feel genuine and evolve quickly. He explains how to define purpose, positioning, and personality, then turn them into useful tools like messaging, visual direction, and a steady customer experience. You’ll gain a simple, repeatable system to guide your brand as it grows.

snippet.title: Create, Partner, Scale: Your Complete Business Playbook
snippet.description:
In 2026, the line between a creator and a business owner has blurred. Small businesses are no longer just advertisers. They are content engines that show up daily across social platforms to attract attention, build trust, and drive sales.

In this conversation hosted by Fast Company, leaders from Constant Contact, TikTok, and Meta break down both sides of the modern marketing equation: how to adopt a creator mindset yourself and how to build mutually beneficial partnerships with creators.

From viral moments and TikTok Shop, to Meta’s creator marketplace and email and SMS that turn followers into repeat customers, this session breaks down the practical systems small businesses use to turn attention into measurable revenue.

Expect real examples, clear trends, and actionable takeaways you can apply right away, whether you're building your own content engine, exploring creator partnerships, or (ideally) doing both.

snippet.title: Introducing Canva AI 2.0 | Canva Create 2026
snippet.description:
Meet your new creative partner. Canva AI 2.0 brings everything you need together in one place. 

It features nine capabilities that will save you countless hours and transform the way you work.

1. Design through conversation: Simply talk through what you need to turn rough concepts into polished, professional results. 

2. Agentic Orchestration: It can now decide on images, text, fonts, colors, and even layouts on your behalf.

3. Memory Library: Intelligent design that learns from you, and gets smarter and more personal with every project you create.

4. Layered Object Intelligence: Generate fully layered designs where every text box, image, and graphic is editable, so you retain total creative control.

5. Canva AI Connectors: It creates what you need using context from apps you use every day, like Slack, Gmail, Google Drive, or your Calendar.

6. Scheduling: Schedule tasks to run automatically, putting work on autopilot even while you’re offline.

7. Web Research: Let it do the research for you and pull what you need from the web directly into your design.

8. Brand Intelligence: It automatically applies your brand to anything you create, so every design is on-brand by default.

9. Canva Code 2.0: Bring any HTML or code file into Canva, and it becomes fully editable. Add forms that collect responses, interactive designs, and more.

Watch the next video to see how you can use all these features at work or for play.

Want to dive straight in? Explore our latest launches at canva.com/launches

snippet.title: World Models Change Everything: Runway Co-Founder
snippet.description:
AI is changing who gets to create and what storytelling can be. 
Runway Chief Innovation Officer Alejandro Matamala Ortiz joins Cameron to explore how AI video is unlocking a new generation of creators and why the future of storytelling may not be something you just watch.
From enabling anyone to make films to building world models that simulate reality, this conversation explores what happens when creation becomes faster, more accessible, and fundamentally different.
In this episode, they cover:
• Why anyone can be a filmmaker already
• How AI video is moving beyond content into new creative mediums
• What world models are and why they matter
• Why storytelling, not tools, still wins
• How this shift could impact industries far beyond media

Timestamps: 
01:28 The Prompt 
03:29 "If you make great things, if you put love into it, people will come back and they will use it." 
04:31 Creative All Hands 
13:27 AI is expanding creativity to new people who always have stories to tell. 
17:06 World models simulate not just visuals but physics, continuity, and object interaction. 
18:13 World models open new frontiers across entertainment, gaming, and robotics. 
19:26 Models learn how the world works by watching vast data and finding correlations. 
22:26 AIFF.com 
22:57 Reactors are experimenting with new formats combining gaming, VR, and storytelling. 
23:45 More projects are being greenlit due to reduced cost. 
24:15 "Stories will always win." 
25:02 Georges Méliès 
29:26 Building is now so cheap, startups can no longer place just one bet. 
36:33 Sitting researchers next to creatives helps you spot what is worth producing. 
38:18 Every major technology shift created new markets, not eliminated roles. 
38:35 Creative roles are blurring: illustrators become filmmakers, writers start thinking in images. 
39:26 All-Star Creative Team 
42:50 Design Reveal 
44:50 Rapid-Fire

snippet.title: Startups in the AI Era: Peter Deng on What Will Win
snippet.description:
Peter Deng, a visionary product leader turned investor, joins the podcast. Peter helped shape Facebook Messenger, Instagram, and ChatGPT, driving major launches like ChatGPT Enterprise, voice, and memory at OpenAI. 
He is now a General Partner at Felicis, where he backs founders building AI-native companies. In this episode, Peter shares how investors evaluate AI startups today, what separates lasting businesses from surface-level integrations, and what founders must rethink to build companies that hold up over time.

snippet.title: The Fun-First Framework for AI Adoption with Allie K. Miller
snippet.description:
Allie K. Miller has a rare superpower: she makes the cutting edge of AI feel clear, practical, and genuinely fun. Recently named to TIME’s list of the most influential people in AI, Allie has become one of the internet’s most trusted guides—breaking down new models, tools, and workflows for millions, from curious beginners to seasoned builders. In this episode, she joins Cameron Adams to unpack what’s coming next: agentic browsers, “AI-first” reinvention, and why productivity alone can be a trap. Along the way, she shares a simple prompt structure that unlocks better outputs, how to turn fear into agency, and why creativity is often the fastest on-ramp to adoption. Plus: a delightfully weird prediction about how we’ll perceive the world.

Cam's notes on Substack: promptedwithcam.substack.com

Timestamps: 
00:00 - Introduction
01:45 - The Prompt
04:07 - Creative All Hands
13:39 - Use AI to simulate future scenarios when convincing teams to change.
15:30 - Let small teams move ahead instead of waiting for company-wide adoption.
17:37 - Use AI to enable work that was previously impractical to do manually.
20:23 - Use creative AI tasks as an entry point before work use cases.
23:32 - Encourage skeptics to try AI even if they expect to dislike it.
24:40 - Ask permission before introducing AI into group conversations.
26:21 - Try this prompt structure: who you are, your objective, then context.
28:07 - Add goals, fears, constraints, and resources to improve AI responses.
31:29 - Photograph handwritten notes or post-its and upload them as AI context.
43:29 - Use AI to analyze patterns across multiple past conversations.
52:10 - Turn one detailed input into multiple formats like decks or videos.
1:01:08 - Design Reveal
1:02:48 - Key Takeaways

snippet.title: Creative Generalists Will Win the AI Era - Google’s Natalie Piucco Shares Why
snippet.description:
Natalie Piucco, Field CTO at Google Cloud, joins Cameron Adams for a wide-ranging conversation on AI, innovation, and what it really takes to lead through constant change. From her childhood on a banana farm to launching AI-powered products at Google, Natalie shares how creativity, trust, and learning shape high-performing teams.

They explore why AI is a fundamentally creative technology, how psychological safety unlocks faster learning, and why we shouldn’t wait to “feel ready” before exploring what problems we can solve with AI. Natalie also unpacks the art of the possible, from creative simulation and education to agentic AI, and explains why the future belongs to high-agency creative generalists. 

Time Stamps
00:00 - Introduction
01:31 - The Prompt
03:47 - Creative All Hands
07:09 - Create psychological safety so your team can admit what they don't know.
08:25 - Train everyone in Design Thinking. It's low cost and unlocks creativity.
12:09 - Use NotebookLM to turn long documents into podcasts you can learn from.
13:49 - AI is an adult-permission slip to do things differently.
17:55 - Add an AI meeting assistant to every call so you can focus on people.
19:45 - Before doing any task, pause and ask: could AI do this?
24:11 - Define where risk-taking lives in your company. Creativity requires it.
25:25 - Don't just adopt AI tools. Help people build mental models for using them.
28:00 - Use the Progress Principle: count testing, feedback, and killing ideas as wins.
32:09 - Look for AI opportunities in boring, repetitive work like tax or compliance.
37:00 - Start your AI experiments with a clear challenge and the metrics associated with that.
38:07 - Price every problem. What does it cost in money, time, or customers?
40:46 - Use the Moonshot Framework: huge problem, radical solution, breakthrough tech in three circles.
43:32 - Build community and in-person connection. AI makes human trust more valuable.
44:00 - All Star Creative Team
46:30 - Design Reveal
49:21 - Rapid Fire

snippet.title: Inside OpenAI’s Global Expansion with Oliver Jay, Managing Director
snippet.description:
How does one of the world’s fastest growing companies approach international scale? How is localizing AI different than localizing any other product? 

Managing Director of OpenAI International, Oliver Jay, joins Cameron to answer these questions and give us a window into what it takes to deploy AI models globally. Drawing on his experience at Dropbox, Asana, and now OpenAI, Oliver explains why AI adoption follows familiar product-led growth principles but moves dramatically faster, how OpenAI works with governments through its OpenAI for Countries program, and why voice, education, and workforce upskilling must coincide to make  AI accessible worldwide.

Cam’s notes on Substack: promptedwithcam.substack.com

Timestamps
01:12 - The Prompt
03:51 - Creative All Hands
06:24 - When demand is global, execute in parallel, not sequential country rollouts.
07:07 - Familiar interfaces (like chat) can unlock adoption faster than capability alone.
07:56 - Start your day by asking AI to preview meetings and prep.
10:15 - Scale globally with bottoms-up product work and top-down government partnerships.
12:38 - The risk of not having enough compute far outweighs the risk of having too much.
13:38 - Upskilling needs systems: academy, certification, and job matching loops.
16:02 - Watch usage patterns by country, product breakthroughs can start anywhere.
16:48 - Design educational AI like a tutor: prompt, challenge, and guide, don't solve.
19:13 - Teach models language principles, and they generalize beyond training languages.
23:22 - Voice can replace keyboards as the gateway to digital opportunity.
26:23 - Traditional teams can lead innovation when AI removes their biggest bottlenecks.
27:55 - Show customers real prototypes fast. Codex can build demos in minutes.
43:48 - All Star Creative Team
45:20 - Design Reveal
47:16 - Rapid Fire
49:02 - Key Takeaways

snippet.title: One Print, One Tree | Malawi Dzalanyama Forest Reserve
snippet.description:
Malawi's Dzalanyama Forest Reserve is facing a significant threat of deforestation. This is due to the production of illegal charcoal, a primary energy source for around 90% of Malawi citizens. While more electric infrastructure is a long-term goal, our work in Malawi focuses on addressing the dual challenge of conserving the forest while meeting charcoal demands. The project envisions long-term environmental and local livelihood benefits by educating communities and implementing sustainable planting and management strategies.

🖨️ About One Print, One Tree:
For every print order placed with Canva, we plant a tree – it’s a simple idea with a big impact. Learn more about the program at https://www.canva.com/one-print-one-tree/

snippet.title: One Print, One Tree | Project FOREST in Tanzania
snippet.description:
In partnership with the Tanzania Forest Service and local NGOs, Canva Print is involved in the Project FOREST initiative.
The project aims to restore forests, enhance water sources, and promote sustainable practices in Tanzania’s Usambara Mountains, a critical hotspot for global biodiversity. The planting methodologies involve establishing community tree nurseries, implementing afforestation programs with local species, and diversifying livelihoods through climate-resilient agriculture.

🖨️ About One Print, One Tree:
For every print order placed with Canva, we plant a tree – it’s a simple idea with a big impact. Learn more about the program at https://www.canva.com/one-print-one-tree/

snippet.title: One Print, One Tree | Project ReGAIN in the Philippines
snippet.description:
Once nearly completely covered with forest, the Philippines has dwindled to less than 20% of its original coverage. To help address this, Canva Print has partnered with the Philippine Eagle Foundation to establish Project ReGAIN. Based in the Davao region, the project is working with the Indigenous Obu Manuvu tribe to restore their ancestral domain and to combat biodiversity loss in the area’s diminishing ancient forests.

🖨️ About One Print, One Tree:
For every print order placed with Canva, we plant a tree – it’s a simple idea with a big impact. Learn more about the program at https://www.canva.com/one-print-one-tree/

snippet.title: Is AI Wired for True Collaboration with Australians? | Provocative Panel Discussion
snippet.description:
Can AI truly collaborate with Australians, or are cultural challenges holding us back? 

This provocative panel from Canva's AI Vision event tackles the hard questions about Australia's AI adoption and innovation future.
Hosted by Shalailah Medhora (Triple J Hack), this panel of industry leaders—including Sherif Mansour (Atlassian), Pier Luigi Caluzzo (Macquarie), Marie-Celine (Made This), and JJ Fiasson (Canva/Leo.AI)—explores the cultural clash threatening Australia's competitive edge in AI integration.

This isn't about AI hype—it's about the real barriers, mindset shifts, and cultural changes needed for meaningful AI collaboration.

Essential viewing for Australian business leaders, innovators, and anyone invested in our nation's tech future.

snippet.title: Reshaping AI Adoption: Cameron Adams in Conversation with OpenAI's Oliver Jay
snippet.description:
How are consumer and business trends reshaping AI adoption globally? Cam Adams sits down with Oliver Jay, Managing Director International at OpenAI, for a headliner conversation exploring the future of innovation and AI responsibility.

This high-level discussion examines how organizations and individuals are approaching AI adoption worldwide, revealing the trends that separate leaders from followers. From consumer behavior shifts to enterprise transformation, this conversation provides the strategic insights needed to navigate AI's rapidly evolving landscape.

Essential viewing for business leaders, innovators, and strategists shaping the future of AI adoption.

snippet.title: The Fourth Industrial Revolution: Building the Infrastructure of Infinite Creativity
snippet.description:
Technology alone won’t define the next industrial revolution, human imagination will. NextDC CEO and Managing Director, Craig Scroggie shares a sweeping vision of how AI, data and exponential technology tools are laying the foundations for a world of infinite creativity.
Craig explores how breakthroughs in computing, driven by GPUs and large language models, are unlocking the AI era where anyone can create, invent and imagine without limits. As Kurzweil’s Law accelerates faster than ever, Craig reveals how unlimited computing power will redefine human potential, shifting us from labour to liberation, from automation to imagination, from self-driving cars to composing symphonies.
This is the infrastructure of infinite creativity, the architecture of a world where technology expands, not replaces, what it means to be human. Technology will create the tools, but it’s people who create the future.

snippet.title: Canva's Two-Step Plan
snippet.description:
Canva has always been guided by a simple but ambitious Two-Step Plan:

1. Build one of the world’s most valuable companies.
2. Do the most good we can.This vision has shaped everything we do — from making design accessible to all, to creating meaningful global impact.

Our impact so far:

- $1.5B+ in product value donated to students, teachers, and nonprofits.
- 800,000 nonprofit teams using Canva Pro for free to amplify their missions.
- 12 million trees planted through our One Print, One Tree program.
- $100M committed to GiveDirectly, supporting 185,000 people living in extreme poverty through direct cash transfers.

But this is only the beginning. We believe in the power of imagination — and in imagining not just better tools, but a better world. A world where everyone’s basic needs are met. A world where global goals reflect the hopes of real people, not just policymakers.
